requirement: The requirements index MUST list examples as well as requirements, identify each entry's kind, and show each example's evidence state. Example detail pages and their links MUST follow {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages` and {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; references to an example MUST link to its definition.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.examples.index`, including its application of the cited `requirements.index.detail_pages` and `requirements.index.navigation`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request any implementation source.

**Index lists examples and identifies each entry's kind**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages]` asserts that the index has rows for the examples `rules.pending` and `rules.missing`, each ending in `(example)`. It also asserts that the requirement row `rules.ready` ends in `(requirement)`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` checks that the default index contains both `(requirement)` and `(example)`.

**Each example's evidence state is shown**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_and_detail_pages_show_each_example_evidence_state]` builds five examples: valid, pending (false), FIXME, changed text, and missing.
- For each one it finds the index row and asserts the state cell exactly: `Recorded true`, `Recorded false`, `Recorded FIXME`, `Recorded true` for the changed case, and `Missing`.
- It also asserts the matching `alt="evidence {state}"` on each example's detail page.
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages]` additionally asserts `alt="evidence Missing"` on the missing example's detail page.

**Example detail pages follow `detail_pages`**
- The default-index test in `src/lib.rs` asserts the detail pages' order and names: `rules.zeta`, `rules.alpha` (an example), `rules.cli.mdbook`, `rules.child.nested`. These are definition order, full-name titles, and subchapters of the index.
- It also asserts each page's parent name and section number.
- It checks that the generated index sits at `requirements-index.md`, which fixes the path the detail pages derive from.

**Navigation for examples**
- The badge links to its own anchor: `id="habeas-example-rules.pending" href="#habeas-example-rules.pending"` in `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages]`. The default-index test checks the same for `alpha`.
- The separate detail link and its icon are covered by the `habeas-detail-icon` assertion and the `requirements-index/...html` href assertions. The test also asserts that no "See evidence" plaintext link is present.
- Each detail page links back to the index: `[Requirements index](../requirements-index.html)` is asserted on all detail pages, including the example's.
- Each detail page links back to the definition: `[View definition](../rules.html#habeas-example-rules.pending)` is asserted for the example.
- The `.md` name case is exercised on a requirement (`cli%2Emdbook`). The text names that case only for requirement names, so no separate example case is needed.

**References to an example link to its definition**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` has a `{test}` reference in another chapter (`guides/deep.md`) to `requirements.something.foo`. It asserts the href `../requirements.html#habeas-example-requirements.something.foo`.
- It also asserts the example badge's own id and alt text.

Together these tests assert exact outcomes for the listing, the kind labels, every evidence-state variant, the detail pages and links, and the reference links. No gap was found.

text: The requirements index MUST list examples as well as requirements, identify each entry's kind, and show each example's evidence state. Example detail pages and their links MUST follow {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages` and {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; references to an example MUST link to its definition.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
